title: Trace Inspector: Filter-first Interaction Explorations
body:
Context and goal:
Goal: Explore a filter-first Trace Inspector UI that surfaces high-signal spans quickly for incident investigation and feature-level debugging. Focus on interaction permutations for filtering, lightweight span grouping, and trace timeline scrubbing that work well with sampled or partial traces.

High-level problem statements (things we heard in CS / SRE interviews):
- Investigators want to find the likely failing service/span within 3 clicks, not scan a 200-span waterfall.
- Current filter controls are buried behind side panels; users often apply ad-hoc queries or export to logs.
- Need quick pivot from a long trace to a minimal reproducible sequence (critical spans).

Exploration notes (sketch ideas and rationale):
1) Filter rail as primary affordance (left-aligned collapsible):
   - Mini-rail sits left of waterfall, visible by default on wide screens.
   - At the top: quick-presets (errors-only, long-tails, high-latency services, cache-misses).
   - Below: attribute search (service:, op:, http.status_code:, component:, tag:).
   - Each filter yields an inline count badge (approx matches) and a fast preview pill that when hovered highlights matching spans in the waterfall.
   - Rationale: reduces context-switch from searching to scanning the waterfall; preview lowers trial-and-error.

2) Preview-on-hover and instant highlight:
   - Hovering a filter pill temporarily overlays a soft highlight on matched spans, and shows an inline micro-summary (avg latency, count, sample trace ids).
   - Click to pin the filter. Pinned filters become chips above the waterfall and persist in the URL.
   - Accessibility: keyboard focus on pills should show same preview and allow pin with Enter.

3) Dynamic grouping and condensation:
   - Group spans by service/op by default with subtle fold arrows.
   - Condensed mode reduces sibling spans into a stacked bar with aggregate latency and error rate. Click to expand.
   - Add an option to auto-group by trace stage (e.g., frontend / auth / db) using lightweight heuristics from tags.

4) Timeline scrubbing + mini-map:
   - Persistent mini-map below header with a draggable viewport for the visible time window.
   - Dragging updates waterfall in real time (throttled) and shows a small sparkline of request-rate over time.
   - Keyboard: left/right arrow nudges viewport by 5% with Shift for 20%.

5) Span-focus pane (right column):
   - Clicking a span opens a focus pane with full span JSON, tags, logs, and raw payload.
   - Add a small "Related traces" row showing other traces with the same error/signature.
   - Allow quick actions: open issue, copy span id, open in lightweight trace diff.

6) Trace diff starter:
   - Select two spans or two traces and launch a side-by-side lightweight diff that emphasizes structural differences (missing spans, timing deltas, different error tags).

Backlog grooming items (rough prioritization):
- P0: Filter rail MVP (pin/unpin, pills, counts, preview-on-hover, URL persistence).
  - Acceptance: a user can apply a filter and see only matching spans; filter state encoded in shareable URL.
- P1: Mini-map + scrubbing (desktop only first).
  - Acceptance: scrubbing updates visible waterfall window without full page reload.
- P1: Keyboard-first interactions for filter rail and span focus.
- P2: Condensed grouping mode and heuristics-based auto-group.
- P2: Related-traces suggestions in span-focus pane (backend dependency: precomputed signatures).
- P3: Trace-diff prototype (afters first two phases).

Edge cases & constraints:
- Sampled traces: counts reported in filter pills should be annotated (e.g., "~12 sampled") and explain interpretation.
- Very wide traces (1000+ spans): default to condensed mode and lazy load DOM; avoid full render.
- Missing timestamps/clock skew: show a warning ribbon and fall back to relative ordering rather than absolute timeline.
- Long tag keys/values: truncate with full tooltip; allow copy.

Microcopy suggestions:
- Filter pill empty state: "No spans match this filter in the current sample window". Add a subtle hint: "try widening time range or remove sampling filter".
- Highlight hover tooltip: show three numbers: count, median latency, error rate. Avoid large tables.

Accessibility & keyboard flows (first pass):
- Tab sequence: left filter rail -> pinned chips -> waterfall canvas -> span list (if condensed) -> span-focus pane.
- All filter pills reachable by arrow keys; Enter to pin, Space to preview (for screen reader parity).
- Provide high-contrast view setting and increased hit-targets for dense spans.

Performance considerations (engineering notes):
- Use incremental rendering by time-window and virtualized span list.
- Server should support pre-computed facet counts per time-bucket for fast pill badges; fall back to approximate counts.
- Preview-on-hover should use cached facet results; if not available show spinner then cancel if mouse moves.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we combine attribute search and free-text logs search in the same rail or separate? (Pros: unified; Cons: cognitive overload). Recommendation: start unified but visually separate (two panels).
- How aggressive should auto-group heuristics be? Users might miss low-level spans. Provide a clear toggle and memory per-user.
- URL complexity: pinned filters + time window + condensed state -> long URLs. Consider short state tokens for share links.

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
- Week 0: Quick whiteboard session with Eng (Diego) and SRE (Ruth) to validate feasibility for preview counts API and sample annotations.
- Week 1: High-fi wireframes for filter rail + pinned chips + hover preview (design).
- Week 2: Spike: implement pill counts API + front-end stub for hover preview (eng infra).
- Week 3: Usability test with 3 CS/SRE customers on a synthetic 200-500 span trace.

Notes to self / miscellaneous scraps:
- Consider a "save investigation" feature that snapshots applied filters + selected spans so an incident can be re-opened. Low priority but high value for on-call handoffs.
- Slack threads: reference #console ux 2025-08-19 where users complained about buried filters.
- Align naming: in copy use "span-focus" consistently rather than mixing "details pane" / "right rail".

Conservative mock labels for designers (for Figma):
- Left rail: "Filter Rail (presets, attributes)"
- Top chips area: "Pinned Filters"
- Center: "Waterfall Canvas (condensed|expanded)"
- Bottom: "Mini-map / Timeline"
- Right: "Span Focus"

Acceptance criteria (detailed for P0):
- Users can apply and pin at least 3 filter types (service, op, error) and see counts.
- Hovering a pill highlights spans without reloading the trace.
- Pinned filters are shareable via URL and restore state on reload.
- On traces > 500 spans, UI defaults to condensed mode and still allows pin/preview interactions.

Approx effort estimate (triaged with Eng):
- Design: 3 designer-weeks (wireframes, hi-fi, hand-off)
- Front-end: 6 engineer-weeks (rail, pills, preview, URL state)
- Backend: 2 engineer-weeks (facet counts + preview API; approximate counts ok)

Final rough mock: ASCII quick frame (for devs to grok ordering)
[ FILTER RAIL ] | [ PINNED CHIPS ]
               | [ WATERFALL (condensed) ]
               | [ MINI-MAP ]
               | [ SPAN FOCUS ]

If design time/eng bandwidth limited: launch a deprecated-simple variant that places filters above the waterfall as a horizontal strip (no preview, no left rail). Use this as an A/B to validate usage pattern before full rail.

End of notes.
